description: Given two strings s and p, return an array of all the start indices of p's anagrams in s. An anagram is a rearrangement of all the characters of a string.
examples:
Input: s = "cbaebabacd", p = "abc"
Output: [0,6]
Explanation: Substrings starting at index 0 ("cba") and index 6 ("bac") are anagrams of "abc".
intuition: This is the same core idea as Permutation in String (567) -- an anagram is just a permutation, meaning identical character frequencies. Slide a window of size len(p) across s, and at each position check if the character frequencies match. The 'matches' counter incrementally tracks agreement across all 26 letters, so each slide costs O(1) instead of O(26).
approach: Use a fixed-size sliding window of length len(p). Maintain frequency counts for the window and for p, with a 'matches' counter tracking how many of the 26 characters have equal frequencies. When matches equals 26, record the start index.
jsWalkthrough:
s = "cbaebabacd", p = "abc"

pCount: a=1, b=1, c=1, rest=0
Initial window "cba": sCount: a=1, b=1, c=1, rest=0
matches = 26 (all 26 positions match)

i=3 (slide to "bae"):
  matches===26 → push 3-3=0 into result. result=[0]
  add "e": sCount[e] 0→1, pCount[e]=0, now 1≠0, matches=25
  remove "c": sCount[c] 1→0, pCount[c]=1, now 0≠1, matches=24

i=4 (slide to "aeb"): matches=24, no push
  add "b": sCount[b] 1→2, pCount[b]=1, now 2≠1, matches=23
  remove "b": sCount[b] 2→1, pCount[b]=1, now equal, matches=24

... (continue sliding)

i=9 (slide to "bac"):
  matches reaches 26 → push 9-3=6 into result. result=[0,6]

return [0, 6]
explanation: Initialize frequency arrays for p and the first window of s. Count initial matches (characters with equal frequency). Slide the window: adding a character may create or break a match; removing a character does the same. Check both transitions. When matches == 26, all frequencies are equal and the window is an anagram. Record its start index.
hints: An anagram has the same character frequencies -- compare frequency arrays instead of sorting.
Use a fixed-size sliding window of length len(p) over s.
Track a 'matches' counter so you do not need to compare all 26 characters each step.
